sermon.title: The Gospel Shaped Life 01/21/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that John, Jesus, the twelve and the seventy all preached the same gospel: repent, be baptized and believe, and receive the Holy Spirit. Groups have made religions of parts of it. Without a gospel-shaped life the door is shut, as in Luke 13 and the ten virgins. With it come peace and the power to bear trials.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A congregant’s name is in the transcript only. Kept as spoken: “Revelations 9 17” (he then reads Revelation 19:7); 1 Peter 4:12 called “fiery darts.” Points to check: Khrushchev memorized the Pentateuch (14:00); a papal paper justifying Southern Catholic slaveholding (28:25); “52% of Christians getting divorced” (54:15); “90% of the people in the Bible” never spoke in tongues (27:00). Sensitive content kept as spoken: Mormons and Muslims “destroying a lot of people” (15:10); “unconditional love nonsense”; tongues-for-salvation “scripturally idiotic”; Jesus-name-only and holiness groups; fundamentalists said tongues are “of the Devil”; Southern denominations embraced slavery; “not for today” is “a total lie.”

Beloved, do not think it strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened to you; but rejoice to the extent that you partake of Christ’s sufferings, that when His glory is revealed, you may also be glad with exceeding joy.

No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.
